target: cohort-excess market return of the anchor board

composite.verdict: no effect detected (mean rho +0.023 over 11 non-overlapping folds; 8/11 folds positive; beat market-value benchmark in 2/11)

momentum.verdict: inconsistent across folds (mean rho -0.123 over 8 non-overlapping folds; 7/8 folds negative; beat market-value benchmark in 0/8)

decision.recommendation: set the momentum weight to zero
decision.rationale: composite mean rho +0.023 vs mispricing +0.023 (delta +0.000); composite beat mispricing in 0/11 folds. The axis does not improve on the component already validated, so it must not move scores. Note this returns the board to ONE live component, which puts Strong labels out of reach again — that is the design working, not a regression.

caveats: Measures Opportunity as it ships OUTSIDE production: the momentum axis alone. The snapTrend axis reads data/playerctx/snapshot.json, which has no history in the repo and cannot be replayed, so it remains unvalidated.
Sharp Flow is absent throughout — the ledger is empty in every reachable environment — so this is a two-component composite.
Replays today's pipeline over past inputs: inputs cannot leak, but the model is current.
Measures market movement, not fantasy production — the panel covers an offseason.
Folds are non-overlapping; the fold count is the honest sample size.

Fewer folds than the mispricing-only backtest, because the lookback window reserves the first 30 days of the panel as history. The head-to-head is still like-for-like: every series in a run is scored on the same folds and the same player intersection.
correction: The caveat below stating that the snapTrend axis 'cannot be replayed' was WRONG, and is corrected in the superseding run. nflverse publishes snap counts per player per game, so the history was always upstream and the playerctx parsers were discarding it; src/playerctx/asof.py bounds the read to the weeks completed before each origin. The axis IS replayable. What it is not, on this panel, is measurable across folds — every offseason date resolves to the same completed season, so it is one frozen cross-section. See ADR-026. Every measured number in this file is unchanged and remains attributable to the run that produced it.
